title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-22
notes:
West leads the ♠7 against 3NT. The opening spade lead is ducked in the dummy. When East produces the ♠J it seems natural for South to win the ♠Q.

There are 8 top tricks (2 spade tricks due to the lead, 3 heart tricks, and 3 diamond tricks). Only the club suit offers any prospect of a ninth trick. West is marked with long spades headed by the ♠K. The contract will be in danger only if West has 5 or more spades.

The ♣A and ♣K rate to be split between the defenders' hands. East will be able to win the first defensive club trick and return a spade through South's ♠10. The ♠A will be driven out and West will still have a club entry to cash out the spade suit.

South can guard against this distribution by ducking East's ♠J at trick 1. As West is marked with the ♠K, South still retains a double stopper. East will return a spade, but when East wins the first club lead he will not have any spades left to drive out South's second stopper.

South may go down by playing this way when West has both the ♣A and ♣K. However, it is more likely that the club honours will be split and South should guard against that possibility.
